title: Noether Symmetries Generate Deterministic Energy-Harvesting Protocols
authors: Ali Akil, M. Hamed Mohammady, Zihan Wang, Oscar Dahlsten
abstract: We consider the general principles for when deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is possible. DEH means absorbing energy from a fluctuating source without entropy being absorbed. We show that the symmetry structure of the source--harvester dynamics gives a general route beyond existing examples to identify DEH capable source states. Any continuous symmetry with a conserved Noether charge induces a source-side orbit of states that all implement the same deterministic harvester transition, provided the harvester boundary states are symmetry invariant. Consequently, one DEH capable source state with nonzero asymmetry between charge sectors can generate infinitely many simultaneously DEH capable source states. A Jaynes-Cummings model, a three-spin XX chain, and an SU(2) model illustrate the construction. We further extend Noether's theorem to generalised probabilistic theories and thereby generalise our main result. We further establish an asymmetry bound for harvesting, showing that source asymmetry cannot increase on average, while DEH saturates the bound exactly preserving asymmetry.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes that the symmetry structure of a quantum source-harvester system dictates whether deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is possible. By applying Noether's theorem, the authors prove that a single symmetry can generate an infinite family of source states, all of which perform the identical energy transfer. This provides a powerful, general framework for understanding energy extraction constrained by fundamental symmetries.
main_problem: The paper seeks to determine the general, symmetry-based conditions under which deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is possible in source-harvester quantum dynamics.
main_result: The existence of a continuous Noether symmetry in the joint dynamics guarantees that an entire orbit of source states will implement the exact same deterministic energy harvesting transition.
method: The authors utilize Noether's theorem, extending it to generalized probabilistic theories, to link continuous symmetries (conserved Noether charges) to the realization of deterministic energy transfer.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a composite Hamiltonian $H = H_h + H_s + H_{int}$, describing the interaction between a 'harvester' subsystem and a 'source' subsystem. Examples include Jaynes-Cummings and SU(2) models.
key_observables: Deterministic output state ($ho_f^h$), source asymmetry ($I$), and the conserved Noether charge ($Q_\alpha$).
important_parameters: The symmetry generator $g$, the time evolution $	au$, and the resonance condition ($\Omega = \omega$) in the classical limit.
main_assumptions: The primary theorems assume the existence of an exact Noether symmetry for the joint dynamics and exact invariance of the harvester boundary states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the generation of DEH-capable source states via symmetry orbits (Figure 1) and show population dynamics confirming the coincidence of outcomes for different symmetry-rotated source states (Figure 2).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining DEH and establishing the general principle using Noether's theorem (Theorem 1), providing concrete quantum examples (Jaynes-Cummings, SU(2)), generalizing the framework to classical and probabilistic theories, and finally deriving constraints on source asymmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general mathematical tool (Noether's theorem) to constrain non-equilibrium processes like energy harvesting, linking fundamental symmetries directly to thermodynamic constraints in open quantum systems.
